content: # Chicago Stadium. | Chicago Blackhawks (NHL) (1929–1994) Chicago Stags (BAA/NBA) (1946–1950) Chicago Majors (ABL "American Basketball League (1961–1963)")) (1961–1963) Chicago Bulls (NBA) (1967–1994) Chicago Sting (NASL "North American Soccer League (1968–1984)")/MISL "Major Indoor Soccer League (1978–1992)")) (1980–1988) | |. **Chicago Stadium** was an indoor arena in Chicago from 1929 to 1995, located at 1800 West Madison Street "Madison Street (Chicago)"). When it was built, it was the largest indoor arena in the world with a maximum seating capacity of 26,000. It was the home of the National Hockey League's Chicago Blackhawks and the National Basketball Association's Chicago Bulls. In sports, it gained the nickname, the "Madhouse on Madison", and a feature during events was the playing of the largest Barton pipe organ ever built. The Stadium hosted the Chicago Blackhawks of the NHL from 1929 to 1994 and the Chicago Bulls of the NBA from 1967 to 1994.

title: Stadium - Wikipedia
content: # Stadium. A **stadium** (pl.: **stadiums** or **stadia**) is a place or venue for (mostly) outdoor sports, concerts, or other events and consists of a field or stage completely or partially surrounded by a tiered structure designed to allow spectators to stand or sit and view the event. Pausanias noted that for about half a century the only event at the ancient Greek Olympic festival was the race that comprised one length of the stadion "Stadion (unit)") at Olympia, where the word "stadium" originated. Most of the stadiums with a capacity of at least 10,000 are used for association football. Many large sports venues are also used for concerts. The English use of *stadium* comes from the tiered infrastructure surrounding a Roman track of such length. The excavation and refurbishment of the stadium was part of the legacy of the Greek national benefactor Evangelos Zappas, and it was the first ancient stadium to be used in modern times.

It opened in 1998 and is home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers of the National Football League (NFL) and the University of South Florida (USF) Bulls college football program. Besides serving as the home field for the Buccaneers and the Bulls, the facility has been the site of three Super Bowls: XXXV in 2001, XLIII in 2009, and LV in 2021, the third of which the Buccaneers became the first team in NFL history both to play and to win a Super Bowl on their home field.
